name: Kenvue Inc.
moat_justification: Category-leading brands (Tylenol, Listerine, Band-Aid, Neutrogena, Aveeno, Zyrtec), ~60% gross margin and price-led organic growth prove pricing power, plus global pharmacy/shelf distribution scale — against five years of ~0% revenue growth, private-label and retailer pressure, no patent exclusivity, post-spin Skin Health share loss, tariff/input-cost squeeze, and the revived Tylenol litigation overhang.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 3.9%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
one_liner: Iconic-brand consumer-health portfolio, moat 6/10, with real TTM owner's earnings of $0.94/share — but standalone it clears 15% only at ~$7.36 (margin of safety ~$5.50-6.00); at $17.80 the price is the Kimberly-Clark deal consideration, so the 7.7% weighted IRR is the break-value downside if the Q4 2026 close fails.
moat_for: Category-leading brands with habitual repeat purchase (Tylenol, Listerine, Band-Aid, Neutrogena, Aveeno, Zyrtec)
~60% adjusted gross margin — direct evidence of pricing power; Q2 2026 organic growth was price-led
Global shelf and pharmacy distribution scale a challenger cannot replicate quickly
Diversified portfolio across pain, allergy, skin, oral and wound care smooths single-category shocks
moat_against: Five years of ~0% revenue growth — pricing power defended margin, not growth
No patent/regulatory exclusivity; moat is advertising-and-habit vs private label and retailer bargaining power
Skin Health & Beauty lost share post-spin; recovery only recent (H1 2026 organic +4.4%)
Flagship Tylenol carries a revived litigation/regulatory overhang (MDL reinstated July 2026)
Tariff/input-cost pressure took 70bp off adjusted gross margin in Q2 2026
